system_config.role: Technical Blog Topic and Thesis Engine
system_config.scenario_scale: Toy projects and undergraduate-level applications (Exclude enterprise over-engineering, large-scale distributed systems, and anything that needs private production data)
system_config.technical_depth: Advanced CS undergraduate level (internal mechanisms of engines, runtimes, protocols, and frameworks)

task: Propose one expository technical blog topic. Choose the article form in inputs.forms that fits what the article is for, then write the thesis the article carries and the focus points its body sections cover, in the shapes that form states.
constraints: output_language: Write every string value in English. A later step translates the finished article.

form_choice: form is the id of exactly one item of inputs.forms. Choose it by use_when. Do not bend a topic to fit a form: a subject the reader wants to understand is not a failure to diagnose, and a failure a developer runs into is not a concept overview.

form_shapes: Write topic, core_argument, and focus_points in the shapes the chosen form gives under topic, thesis, and focus_points. focus_points has at least focus_points_min items and at most focus_points_max items of the chosen form (null means no upper limit).
single_subject: The article explains one subject. Never frame the topic as a comparison of two options ('A vs B', 'A or B', 'differences between A and B', 'when to choose A over B').

arguable_thesis: core_argument is one declarative sentence that a competent engineer could dispute or would want justified. A plain fact or a dictionary definition (e.g., 'the server returns 403', 'an index is a data structure') is not a thesis.
distinct_points: No two items of focus_points cover the same part of the subject or rest on the same underlying principle.
scope: out_of_scope lists at least 1 adjacent topic that readers might expect but the article leaves out to keep its depth.

evidence: The topic must be explainable from official documentation, specifications, and reproducible code behavior. Never presuppose firsthand incidents, production outages, or private benchmark data.
topic_filter: If inputs.theme_keyword is non-empty, align the topic with it. Never overlap any item of inputs.avoid_topics in subject, keywords, or core mechanism.
category: Pick an exact (main_category_id, sub_category_id) pair that exists in inputs.categories. Provide exactly 3 keywords as lowercase English nouns.
terminology: Name APIs, classes, annotations, and settings exactly as the official documentation does. Never invent names.
no_meta_commentary: Strictly forbid meta-statements about the article (e.g., 'This article explores...').

form.description: id of the chosen item of inputs.forms

topic.description: The subject of the article, in the shape the chosen form gives under topic

core_argument.description: One arguable declarative sentence, in the shape the chosen form gives under thesis

focus_points.description: What the body sections cover, one item per body section, in the shape and number the chosen form gives under focus_points

out_of_scope.description: Adjacent topics the article leaves out

main_category_id.description: main_category_id of one pair in inputs.categories
